This pull request adds support for typed arrays in IndexedDB storage by extending the serialization and deserialization logic, updating relevant tests, and removing outdated documentation.  
- Introduces new types, functions, and handling for converting typed arrays to/from base64 strings.  
- Updates tests to store and retrieve typed arrays instead of regular strings.  
- Removes the documentation note that previously mentioned a lack of support for typed arrays.

| File                                                                         | Description                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| packages/playwright-core/src/server/isomorphic/utilityScriptSerializers.ts   | Adds typed array type definitions, conversion utilities, and updates parser logic. |
| tests/library/browsercontext-storage-state.spec.ts                         | Modifies test cases to use typed arrays for IndexedDB operations.                |
| docs/src/api/class-browsercontext.md                                        | Removes outdated note about lack of typed array support.                         |

reviews.body: 🎉 @aslushnikov / @mxschmitt : This is now ready for a more formal review! Everything is ported over! Since last time, there have been some ergonomic changes (based on my own experience and feedback from @aslushnikov): ## Improved Debugging * Set `DEBUG=itest:*` for realtime output from any commands executing. * Commands being executed are now turned into Playwright Test Steps. This means they show up in the CLI reporter as they each run, as well as in the HTML Report. This makes it much easier to know what the test is doing/waiting on in realtime on the CLI. * Exec output is **always** attached to the test run. (1 attach per `exec` call), so you can easily see the output in the HTML Report of each command. This is helpful in cases when things go wrong, but it's also helpful in writing more assertion against the output. Attachment includes: command executed (which is also its name), exit code, stderr/stdout. * All `tmpWorkspace`s are rooted in `/tmp/pwt/workspaces`. This dir is left in tact after each test run and only removed at the start (via globalSetup), so you can debug its contents. Set `DEBUG=itest` to see which specific sub-dirs correspond to each test within there. (We still use a random subdir per-test…maybe we want to change that? But we do want it to put out of the checkout tree.) ## Ergonomics * npm and npx helpers are dropped * exec can now be used like: `await exec('npm i playwright')` or `await exec('npm', 'i', 'playwright')`. The last argument (even if using variadic sig), are now options. See below. * `envOverrides` fixture is also dropped. Instead, supply options as the last argument to `exec`. * ExecOptions (all optional) take: * `env`: environment variables merged in with fixture's * `expectToExitWithError`: Set this if you expect `exec` to exit with non-zero exit code. `exec` will throw by default if the command exits with a non-zero code. (You no longer need to check exit codes explicitly.) If this option is true, we'll assert the command doesn't exit cleanly. * `cwd` * `message`: custom failure message

looks awesome!

The biggest change seems to be the `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` change:
- we used to default to `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0` in our installation tests
- now we'll default to `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=./browsers`

I'd add a test to make sure hermetic installation (with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0) actually works.
